research_concepts: sequential play-type events from NBA play-by-play
methodological_questions: correct temporal ordering of play types within a possession
look-ahead or backfill bias in play-type labeling
reliability of derived DRIVE and PNR labels
confounding from foul-related artifacts in play-type PPPs
whether a preceding DRIVE can be cleanly identified when multiple actions occur

historical_evidence.finding: Defensive scheme change within game and across games could not be tested due to inferred label noise; near-uniform transition matrices consistent with label error.

Play-type label backfill verification: overall FAIL; PNR share 28.7% FAIL, many team PNR rates >33% FAIL; 82.8% of PNR labels proxy-calibrated; team identity check FAIL. Final verdict FAIL, classified as an artifact caused by label/construction flaws.
On-ball defensive scheme labels could not be extracted at usable rates (confident labels 14.9% and 3.3%); switches_on field unpopulated; question deemed untestable.

Play-type PPP differences are primarily labeling artifacts: OTHER PPP inflated by 36% foul endings, DRIVE PPP deflated 12pp below foul benchmark; only 0.7% of possessions map to a real play type via initiation_type.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Effort to validate play-type labels (including PNR) derived from NBA play-by-play and backfill
failed_approaches.why: Label classification error; large proportion of PNR labels are proxy-calibrated, team identity distribution fails, leading to artifact classification (C_artifact).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using derived play-type labels (DRIVE, PNR, OTHER) to evaluate true efficiency differences
failed_approaches.why: Foul leakage creates strong artifactual biases in PPP; DRIVE and PNR labels suffer from foul-related misclassification, making PPP comparisons invalid.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferring defensive scheme changes within and across games from derived labels
failed_approaches.why: Label noise produces near-uniform transition patterns indistinguishable from chance; the question could not be answered with available data (LABEL_ERROR).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labeling on-ball defensive coverage (e.g., DROP/ICE/SWITCH) from NBA matchup/PBP fields
failed_approaches.why: Confident label rate too low (3–15%) and key fields unpopulated; untestable at usable power.

evidence_establishes: Derived play-type labels (DRIVE, PNR) from NBA play-by-play and graph databases contain substantial classification error
PNR labels specifically are largely proxy-calibrated and fail team-identity checks (FAM:SF-APPA-030)
DRIVE and PNR PPP are contaminated by foul-related artifacts, with DRIVE PPP systematically deflated relative to a foul benchmark (FAM:SF-CHT-025)
Label noise can produce patterns that are indistinguishable from chance, even in large samples (FAM:SF-APPA-005)
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR actually raises PNR PPP
Whether the temporal order of DRIVE and PNR within a possession can be accurately captured with current labels
The exact error rates for sequential DRIVE-PNR pairs in the 2025‑26 data
own_inferences: The research question requires a reliable sequence of play types (DRIVE then PNR) within the same possession; given past label failures, the derived labels are unlikely to support this.
Foul artifacts (FAM:SF-CHT-025) that differentially affect DRIVE and PNR PPP would confound any observed effect, making it impossible to separate a real tactical influence from a labeling artefact.
The question is likely untestable unless a radically different play-type classification method (e.g., manual video charting) is introduced.
Even with perfect labels, the estimand would be vulnerable to look‑ahead/backfill bias if the labeling system uses post hoc information to classify preceding actions.
uncertainties: Specific accuracy of DRIVE labels preceding a PNR in the 2025‑26 season has not been measured, although the general label audit indicates pervasive errors.
The proportion of possessions that contain both a teammate DRIVE and a PNR is unknown; the exposure could be very sparse.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved evidence on play-type label quality strongly indicates that DRIVE and PNR labels are too unreliable for the proposed sequential analysis; without this evidence one might have considered a straightforward observational test, but the documented label errors, foul artefacts, and backfill failures make proceeding highly inadvisable.

blocking_constraints.text: Past audits show high classification error for DRIVE and PNR labels, including proxy calibration of PNR labels and foul-related misclassification, making it unlikely that the required sequential labelling is accurate enough.
Foul leakage differentially affects DRIVE and PNR PPP, which would bias the comparison of PNR PPP with vs. without a prior DRIVE.
Play-type labelling may use future events to classify preceding actions; a successful PNR could influence whether an earlier action is labelled as a DRIVE, creating reverse causality.

prior_work.summary: No prior study directly tests the effect of a teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR on PNR PPP. However, multiple investigations of the same derived play-type labels demonstrate pervasive label errors and PPP artefacts that would render such a test invalid.

risks.text: DRIVE and PNR labels have documented high error rates; PNR labels are largely proxy‑calibrated, and DRIVE labels suffer from foul leakage misclassification.
Foul-related artifacts inflate/deflate play-type PPPs, so any observed difference in PNR PPP may be caused by foul leakage rather than a tactical effect of the prior DRIVE.
Play-type classification algorithms may inadvertently use the outcome of a PNR or subsequent events to label earlier actions as a DRIVE, reversing the temporal arrow.
Possessions containing both a leading teammate DRIVE and a PNR may be rare, leading to small effective samples and low power even if labels were perfect.
If the presence of a prior DRIVE is correlated with defensive breakdowns that also affect PNR PPP, regression to the mean of individual possessions could bias estimates.

design.estimand: The difference in PNR points per possession between possessions where a teammate DRIVE (distinct from the PNR ball‑handler) occurred earlier in the same possession and possessions without any prior teammate DRIVE, adjusting for the foul‑related PPP artefact.
design.unit: A possession that contains a PNR action
design.sample: NBA 2025‑26 regular season and playoffs, but only after a rigorous manual‑charting validation of DRIVE and PNR labels on a random subset of possessions; the test would proceed only if label accuracy exceeds a pre‑registered threshold (e.g., Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 for both labels).
design.power: Power cannot be credibly estimated until label quality and exposure prevalence are verified; if fewer than 2 000 qualifying possessions are available, the test would be abandoned for insufficient power.
design.controls: Score margin, period, shot clock, defensive matchup complexity (as manually coded), prior offensive actions in the possession (count of passes, paint touches), and a foul‑ending indicator to mitigate the foul‑artefact confound.
design.falsification: Check that the probability of a prior DRIVE being recorded is not higher when the PNR results in a high‑PPP outcome; if a positive association is found between PNR success and the likelihood of a preceding DRIVE label, the labelling system is considered temporally contaminated and the test is terminated.
design.multiplicity: Single primary hypothesis; no subgroup analyses unless the pre‑registered validation passes; season‑level estimates would be pooled with a hierarchical model to avoid multiple‑testing inflation.
design.decision_rule: Proceed to analysis only after the label validation gate is passed; the hypothesis is supported if the adjusted PNR PPP difference is positive with a 95% credible interval excluding zero, and if the falsification test shows no reverse‑direction bias (p > 0.10).
design.data_version: 2026‑06‑14 snapshot of the graph database, verified against a charting sample.

methodological_questions: data reliability of derived play types
args.query: Any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-14, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}

{"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["DRIVE play type", "PNR (pick and roll) play type", "teammate actions", "sequential possessions", "points per possession", "NBA play-by-play data"], "methodological_questions": ["temporal precedence within possession", "multiple drives before PNR", "look-ahead bias in labeling", "possession-level context", "data reliability of derived play types"], "query": "Any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP"}}

reasoning_details.text:
We need to extract research concepts and methodological questions from the research question. The research question: "Any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP."

Key concepts: play types: DRIVE and PNR (pick and roll). Teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR. Outcome: PNR PPP (points per possession). So we're looking at the effect of a preceding drive by any teammate on the efficiency of a subsequent PNR within the same possession or maybe across possessions? "Preceding" likely means within the same possession, i.e., a possession that includes a drive and then a PNR. The question is whether the presence of a teammate drive before a PNR raises the points per possession of that PNR.

Methodological questions: How to define "preceding"? What is the unit of analysis? Possession? How to link drives and PNRs within a possession. Data quality: play-type labeling from derived play-type possession records. Potential issues: defining when a drive occurs relative to a PNR, ensuring they are part of the same possession, handling multiple drives, etc. Also, confounders: maybe drives that lead to PNRs are different. Risk of selection bias, leakage, etc.

Data catalog: per-game files from NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), etc. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points). So we have play types assigned to possessions. We need to check if the data includes plays like "drive" and "PNR" as play types. Likely, play types are derived from action types. So we need to see if historical research has addressed similar questions.

We need to call retrieve_history with research concepts and methodological questions. The query should summarize the question.

Research concepts: ["DRIVE play type", "PNR (pick and roll) play type", "teammate actions", "sequential possessions", "points per possession", "NBA play-by-play data"]

Methodological questions: ["How to define temporal precedence within a possession?", "How to handle multiple drives before a PNR?", "How to avoid look-ahead bias in labeling drive and PNR?", "How to account for possession-level context?", "Data reliability of derived play types?"]

Query: "Any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP"

Thus the retrieval call.

But we must not assume facts. So just retrieve.

We need to process stage 2. We have retrieval results with 4 records: FAM:SF-APPA-005, FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPS-058, FAM:SF-CHT-025. They are about defensive scheme change, play-type label backfill verification, on-ball defensive scheme labels, and play-type labeling audit OTHER/DRIVE foul leakage. None directly address the research question "Any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP." But they highlight risks and limitations of play-type labeling, especially that play-type labels may have errors (label error), artifacts (foul leakage), and limited labeling quality (low confident label rates, backfill failures). So historical evidence is not directly on the research question but relevant for methodology.

We need to summarize relevant historical findings and failed approaches from these records. For each record, note its status as recorded: 
- FAM:SF-APPA-005: status "untestable" (auto_outcome_status: untestable). Finding: defensive scheme change within game and across games, but question not answerable with data due to label error, near-uniform transition matrices consistent with label noise.
- FAM:SF-APPA-030: status "inconclusive". Finding: play-type label backfill verification failed; PNR 28.7% FAIL, PULL_UP 7.9% FAIL, 3100 games with team PNR >33% FAIL, PNR PPP pass, temporal pass, team identity fail, 2024-25 PULL_UP ~0-1% for many teams. Final: FAIL. Artifact mechanism: C_artifact (label flaw). 82.8% of PNR labels proxy_calibrated.
- FAM:SF-APPS-058: status "untestable". Finding: on-ball defensive scheme labels from NBA matchup/PBP fields could not be labeled at usable rates; confident label rates 14.9% and 3.3%; switches_on unpopulated; failed gate. Risk: label error, small sample.
- FAM:SF-CHT-025: status "artifact". Finding: OTHER PPP inflated by 36% foul endings, DRIVE 12pp below foul benchmark, PNR 22% foul rate; only 0.7% of possessions map to a real play type via initiation_type. Play-type PPP differences are artifacts, not real efficiency. Verdict: artifact_found.

These records establish that derived play-type labels (including DRIVE, PNR) suffer from significant label error and artifacts, making analysis of play-type PPP potentially unreliable. Specifically, FAM:SF-APPA-030 shows that PNR labels themselves have issues, FAM:SF-CHT-025 shows foul leakage artifacts that affect DRIVE and PNR, and FAM:SF-APPA-005 and FAM:SF-APPS-058 indicate label noise. So while none directly tested the question of "teammate DRIVE preceding PNR raises PNR PPP," they indicate that the labeling of both DRIVE and PNR is unreliable, which would confound any attempt to answer the question.

Now steps: 4-9. We need to output final JSON.

We need to list historical_evidence and failed_approaches. For each record, we can include a finding. For failed_approaches, we can mention that approach of labeling play types from PBP data has failed to produce reliable labels (e.g., FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-CHT-025, FAM:SF-APPA-005). We should cite the IDs. Also, we might look at whether any specific failed approach directly addresses the research question. None do. So failed_approaches can cite them as failed attempts to produce reliable play-type labels, which undermine the current question.

Now we must fill all fields. For evidence_establishes: What does the retrieved evidence establish for this question? It establishes that derived play-type labels (DRIVE, PNR) are subject to substantial classification error and artifactual PPP biases (foul leakage, backfill issues), limiting the reliability of any analysis using those labels. It does not directly address the influence of a prior DRIVE on PNR PPP. So summarize.

evidence_does_not_establish: It does not establish whether a teammate DRIVE before a PNR indeed raises PNR PPP, nor does it validate that the DRIVE and PNR labels can be accurately sequenced within a possession.

own_inferences: The research question likely suffers from the same label error and artifact risks, making it likely untestable or artifact-prone. The sequential relationship (preceding DRIVE) adds complexity because closely spaced actions may be mislabeled or not independent. The question may be answerable only if the labeling of DRIVE and PNR is sufficiently accurate, which evidence suggests it is not. So we infer that proceeding would be risky.

uncertainties: We don't know the exact error rates for labeling a "teammate DRIVE" preceding a PNR in the 2025-26 season data, but past audits indicate high failure rates. The question might be more testable if using a different labeling method (e.g., manual charting), but with current derived labels it's doubtful.

historical_effect: Since no historical evidence directly tested the same question, but it provided context on label quality, it might change decision from "proceed" to "do_not_proceed" due to risks. So changed_decision: yes, explanation: prior work on label quality indicates that the play-type classification is too unreliable to support this analysis, causing us to recommend not proceeding.

testability: p_testable: we think very low, say 0.05. Blocking constraints: LABEL_ERROR (play-type label error), also CONFOUNDING because foul artifacts can confound PPP, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD? The question about "preceding" may require ordering within a possession; if labeling uses future information, could be look-ahead bias. But the main issue is label error. So list codes: LABEL_ERROR, RTM_SELECTION? Not sure. We'll also mention CONFOUNDING from foul artifacts. But the block is label error.

prior_work: already_answered: no. cited: list the IDs that inform the decision: FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-CHT-025, maybe FAM:SF-APPA-005. Summary: Prior work on play-type label quality shows pervasive label errors and artifacts, casting doubt on the feasibility of testing the question.

risks: LABEL_ERROR (play types DRIVE and PNR are noisy), CONFOUNDING (foul leakage skews PPP), maybe MEASURE_RELIABILITY (labels are proxy-based), LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD (play type labeling may look ahead to infer types, causing reverse causality if a DRIVE is inferred after a PNR). Mention LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD.

predicted_outcome: probably untestable high, artifact some, low supported/rejected. So:
supported: 0.05, rejected: 0.05, untestable: 0.65, artifact: 0.20, uncertain: 0.05 (but sum 1.0). Adjust: total: 0.05+0.05+0.65+0.20+0.05=1.0.

decision: do_not_proceed.

design: even if do_not_proceed, provide a minimum viable test design. estimand: The difference in PNR points per possession between possessions that had at least one teammate DRIVE in the same possession vs those without any teammate DRIVE, controlling for other factors. unit: a possession (or a PNR possession). sample: NBA 2025-26 regular season/playoffs, but need to exclude possessions with ambiguous labeling. power: not computable due to label noise. controls: game state, shot clock, defensive matchup, location. falsification: check that DRIVE labels are not systematically assigned after a successful PNR (temporal order). multiplicity: multiple testing by season, but can aggregate. decision_rule: pre-registered threshold after label quality audit passes. But given label quality, we should first verify labeling accuracy with manual charting or alternative source. So design notes: cannot proceed with current derived labels.

Now format JSON accordingly. Ensure all fields filled. Use proper codes. I'll produce final.
